scope.summary: Implement the skinning weights authority per Section 13.18 (BK-18.2, TAI-BK-060), closing REQ-020: linear blend skinning (LBS) weights on the base mesh are the authority (weights_artifact_ref, chosen for engine parity), with an optional dual-quaternion (DQS) or blended LBS/DQS PREVIEW mode for the viewport — every export lane bakes from LBS; twist bones (13.18 authority skeleton) carry the candy-wrapper mitigation.
acceptance_criteria: SkinWeights stores per-vertex (bone_index, weight) influence lists normalized to 1.0, versioned against (base_mesh_version, skeleton_version); loading against mismatched versions is a typed error.
LBS skinning evaluates deterministically: pose x weights -> deformed vertices, bit-identical across runs; a golden-pose fixture pins output.

DQS and blended LBS/DQS evaluation exist behind a PreviewSkinning mode flag; authority persistence stores LBS only, and a test asserts export-facing accessors always return LBS-skinned results regardless of preview mode.
Weight validation: influences per vertex within a configurable cap, weights normalized, no references to bones absent from the skeleton version (each violation a typed finding).

Twist-bone weights present on upperarm/lowerarm/thigh/calf twist bones in the seeded weight fixture; a 90-degree forearm twist pose shows reduced volume loss with twist bones vs without (candy-wrapper regression test).
scope.risk_if_missed: DQS-as-authority breaks engine parity (game engines consume LBS) while LBS-without-twist-bones candy-wrappers slender limbs — Daz's TriAx-era lesson; mixing preview and authority skinning would ship bodies that deform differently in UE than in the viewport.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
